articles.title: Plain, specific headline that states what happened (no hype words)
articles.subtitle: One sentence that adds the key number or consequence the title leaves out.
articles.coverImageAlt: What the photo shows, and how it relates to the story

threeQuestions.whatHappened: Who did what, when, with the exact numbers from the primary source. More than 80 characters.
threeQuestions.whyItMatters: The concrete consequence: cost, capability, risk or rule that changes, and for whom. More than 80 characters.
threeQuestions.whatsNext: Named next steps with dates or thresholds to watch, as stated by sources. More than 80 characters.

keyTakeaways: First fact a reader should keep.
content: Source line: what you read (e.g. 'Source: the company's announcement of 11 October 2026 and the arXiv abstract').
Paragraph with facts, figures or mechanisms that are NOT already in threeQuestions.
Another paragraph with new detail, a quote, a timeline, or a counter-argument.
Limits: what is not known yet, what the source does not say.

citations.title: Exact title of the primary source page

briefing.summary: Two sentences that sum up today's top stories.
